live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust ransomware-for-hire gang behind hits on healthcare, casinos and local governments
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran ransomware-as-a-service from late 2021. Affiliates hit hospitals, casinos, cities and firms. Its sites were disrupted in December 2023, and BleepingComputer reported an apparent exit scam in March 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, BlackCat, Ambitious Scorpius and UNC4466. Symantec uses the name Noberus.
It is a ransomware-as-a-service operation. The malware is written in Rust and runs on Windows, Linux and VMware ESXi.
Malpedia says ALPHV has been seen in attacks since November 18, 2021.
Cisco Talos describes the links between BlackCat and the BlackMatter/DarkSide ring as probable. It has moderate confidence that BlackMatter affiliates were early BlackCat adopters.

A BlackCat representative told Recorded Future that the two groups were connected but that BlackCat was not a rebrand of BlackMatter, as Talos recounts. S2W found it difficult to conclude they are the same group.
eSentire says ALPHV and its affiliates are typically seen as Russian-speaking. It adds that various security teams report the core operators are based in Russia, and it does not verify this itself.

Victims named in the reports include Sun Pharmaceuticals, Henry Schein, Constellation Software, loanDepot and Prudential Financial. Local governments such as Suffolk County and the city of Alexandria were also hit.
Recorded Future News says the group has made a point of going after healthcare and pharmaceutical companies.

Cybernews reports that BlackCat listed NJVC, an IT company supporting US government and defense bodies, on its leak site on 28 September 2022. The report treats this as the gang's own claim, and NJVC did not comment.
The ransomware can be set to encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20. It can delete volume shadow copies, stop services and ESXi virtual machines, and spread by using PsExec.
Victims face double extortion. Data is stolen, and the gang threatens to publish it on its leak site if the ransom is not paid.
Symantec says 2022 updates added an ARM build and safe-mode encryption, plus searchable leak sites. It also saw an affiliate use the Eamfo infostealer against Veeam backup credentials.

Sygnia traced one 2023 intrusion to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Access came through a compromised third-party vendor. The attacker then spent weeks moving through the network with Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools, and copied data out with Rclone.
eSentire says Russian-speaking affiliates used Google ads to lure users into downloading the Nitrogen malware, which led to ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware.
ReliaQuest says Scattered Spider has formed alliances with ransomware operators including ALPHV.

BleepingComputer reports that the FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches in its first four months, from November 2021 to March 2022. The FBI also estimates it took at least $300 million in ransoms from more than 1,000 victims up to September 2023.

In a statement about the September 2023 MGM Resorts attack, AlphV said it had kept administrator access to MGM's systems. It also said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors. These are the group's own unverified claims.
Henry Schein disclosed an incident on October 15, 2023. The report says AlphV (BlackCat) claimed it and re-encrypted systems after negotiations broke down.

In the Change Healthcare case, unnamed sources told BleepingComputer the attack was linked to BlackCat. BlackCat had not claimed it at the time, and UnitedHealth's SEC filing blamed a suspected nation-state actor.

In December 2023, an international law enforcement operation seized the gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites. In March 2024, BleepingComputer judged that the gang was running an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and it offered its source code for $5 million.
The same report says a fake FBI seizure banner appeared on the leak site. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved. It is unclear whether the group will return under a new name.
According to a Malpedia reference, on 2025-12-30 the US Justice Department announced that two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.
Treat third-party vendor access and remote management tools as part of your attack surface, and review them often.
Keep backups and backup credentials separate from the main network, and rehearse recovery before an incident.
